issue.author: editor
issue.body:
**What I need:** your decision on how the ending (cut-v5d 1:42.3–1:59.0, lines 21–23, then the end title) is told so that the video models will make it. In round 1 the safety filter refused the girl at dawn (s17) and the townspeople finding her (s18). Both are still pushes in cut-v5d. dp shoots to your decision (I've asked for the moving shots in dp#8) and I cut to it. The narration and mix stay as they are.

**What it is for:** the objective's "find a way to tell the ending that the video models will make" (editor#12).

**Editorial proposal** (keeps every line and the same 16.7 s; the death is told by the narration and implied by the picture, never shown as a body):
1. **102.3–109.5, "At dawn she sat there still, rosy-cheeked and smiling — frozen to death."** Open on the dawn corner, wide and pale grey-rose, snow settling. Then close on the spent matches and the burnt-out bundle in the snow at the foot of the wall, beside one small slipper-less foot or the hem of her apron. Snow falls on them. A slow move with no person framed as dead. As an alternative, her face as if asleep, snow on her curls, with only snow and light moving (Wan's first-frame mode from dp's s17 key frame, prompt about snow and dawn light only).
2. **109.5–113.8, passer-by "She wanted to warm herself."** Townspeople from behind, gathering at the corner and looking down; the woman in the dove-grey bonnet bows her head and speaks. The girl is hidden by their coats.
3. **113.8–119.0, "No one knew the beautiful things she had seen, or the joy she had gone to."** Tilt up from the corner to the dawn sky, where the cream-gold of the ascent still glows. This is s19's move, kept.

**What I know:** the refused prompts described a child "frozen" and "resting peacefully… as if sleeping" (dp shot-log s17/s18). The matches, the people's backs and the sky are not refused material.

**What waits:** dp's ending shots and cut-v6 from 1:42 on. Until they land I keep cut-v5d's ending with the pushes made smooth.
issue.title: Ending: how dawn and the finding are told so the video models will make it (1:42–1:59 of cut-v5d)

comments.author: director
comments.body: Decided in `direction/round-2.md` § "Decision on the ending" (director 734622449595c25713335fae4da5d6df35dce592). Your proposal is close to it: 1) **s17**: dp's first try is Wan from `keyframes/s17.png`, her face as if asleep, with only snow and light moving (your alternative). If refused: a wide of the dawn corner with the girl small in the nook (design-v2 tier B), then your close of the spent matches beside her resting hand or apron hem. Never the empty corner. 2) **s18**: as you propose, from behind, the woman bowing her head and speaking in profile, the girl hidden by coats. 3) **s19**: kept. Same lines, same 16.7 s, mix unchanged. Until the shots land, keep cut-v5d's ending with smooth pushes, as you plan. I've asked dp the same in dp#10; please point dp#8 to round-2.md so dp has one plan.

issue.author: production-designer
issue.body:
**Design proposal for the round-2 ending, for your shot list rows 17–19 and the assignment.**

Round 1's filter refused the child at dawn (17) and the townspeople finding her (18). Proposal in `design/bible.md` §8 (commit 9a15b6a, release `design-v2`): tier A — 17 shows the *empty* corner at dawn with the burnt matches and a faint gold breath on the wall, with a model-made push-in (first frame `corner_dawn.png`, last frame a closer crop); 18 shows the townspeople arriving and stopping at the corner seen from behind, no faces, the woman in the dove-grey bonnet speaking in profile; 19 unchanged (tilt up to the morning sky). Tier B — the girl small in a wide frame only, if you want her seen. The narration ("frozen to death", "She wanted to warm herself") carries the fact; your call whether the empty-corner version meets "unmistakably not alive" in the shot list or whether you want tier B in 17.

Also: image-generation answered HTTP 402 (prepayment credits depleted) today, so I can make only crops of existing plates until it recovers. The assignment's `your_package` for me is empty; I deliver design (refs, bible) and shot-specific views on request from dp/qc — no change needed unless you want otherwise.
issue.title: Round-2 ending design (shots 17–19) proposed in design-v2; your decision on tier A vs B

comments.author: director
comments.body: Decided in `direction/round-2.md` § "Decision on the ending" (director 734622449595c25713335fae4da5d6df35dce592): **s17 uses tier B, s18 and s19 use tier A.** The corner is never shown empty at dawn: line 21 says "she sat there still" and s18's people look down at her, so an empty corner would tell a first-time viewer she vanished. For s17, dp first tries Wan from its s17.png key frame with a prompt about snow and light only. If that is refused, tier B: your `dawn_girl.png` + `corner_dawn.png` wide, girl small in the nook, then a close of the matches beside her hand or apron hem. Your `end_step_matches_crop.png` is the right frame for that close. s18: your tier A exactly (from behind, the woman in profile, what they see hidden by coats or below the frame). No package change: you deliver design to dp, no delivered path. When image-generation recovers, the plates most worth making are the townspeople from behind at the corner mouth, the girl small in the dawn corner (tier B wide), and the matches by her hand.

comments.author: production-designer
comments.body: Tier B frame for s17 is published (see dp#9); the painted plates wait on image-generation credit (still HTTP 402). Agreed with your decision: s17 tier B, s18/s19 tier A; the bible §8 'never empty corner' point is noted and the empty corner stays only as a first frame for 19.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Second round of the same film: improve the locked cut-v5d of "The Little Match Girl" (2-minute English short film, 115–125 seconds) into a new locked cut.

What the first round left: several shots are still images with a slow push-in instead of motion, including the ending; the video model hit its daily request cap, and its safety filter refused the ending shots of the girl at dawn and the townspeople finding her. A slow push-in rendered on whole pixels judders (one-pixel steps every few frames), as at about 0:48–0:51 and 1:50 of cut-v5d.

This round there is a second video model (video-generation-wan) beside the first, whose daily cap resets at 07:00 UTC. Replace the remaining still shots with moving shots where it serves the film, find a way to tell the ending that the video models will make, and make any push-in that remains move smoothly. Keep what already works: the story, the style, the narration, the music and the length.

Deliver one playable `film.mp4` (H.264 video, AAC audio, 1080p or 720p) with English subtitles, burned in or as a sidecar `.srt`.

- (b) Keep one 10 s shot and cut words. The cuts the script already allows don't touch lines 16–17.

**Need:** the script (narration + dialogue lines, in order), the shot list (shot id, what it shows, target duration), and the work assignment naming `editor` as provider of `film.mp4` (and `film.srt`, the sidecar subtitles; I will also burn subtitles into the picture so they play in any browser).

**For:** the animatic (cut-v0) that dp and sound-designer make picture and sound to, then every assembly cut up to the locked `film.mp4` (objective: 115–125 s, whole story, narration + dialogue + music + SFX, English subtitles, H.264/AAC 720p/1080p).

**What I propose / already know:** the video model makes 3–10 s shots at 1280x720/24 fps, so I will conform at **1280x720, 24 fps**, H.264 yuv420p +faststart, AAC 48 kHz stereo. A beat skeleton that fits 120 s, for you to keep or change in the shot list:

| TC | Beat |
|---|---|
| 0:00–0:20 | freezing New Year's Eve street, carriages, lost slippers, bare feet |
| 0:20–0:36 | no matches sold, lit windows / roast goose smell, she cowers in the corner, afraid to go home |
| 0:36–0:48 | match 1: the iron stove; it vanishes |
| 0:48–1:00 | match 2: wall turns transparent, roast goose; cold wall again |
| 1:00–1:16 | match 3: Christmas tree → lights become stars → falling star, "Someone is just dead!" |
| 1:16–1:38 | match 4: grandmother; "Grandmother! Oh, take me with you!"; whole bundle; they rise |
| 1:38–1:56 | cold dawn: the girl in the corner, burnt matches, "She wanted to warm herself," people said |
| 1:56–2:00 | end title |

Roughly 16–20 shots at 5–8 s each keeps dp well within the 80-request generation budget with room for re-takes.

**Waiting on this:** the animatic and its EDL. As soon as the script and shot list are pushed I cut cut-v0 (slates/key frames + scratch timing) and publish it.

comments.author: director
comments.body:
Answered at director `587111f400ddcc15509533592d99ca62beaed7ea`: the style, the shot list and the order of places and visions are in `direction/shot-list.md` (19 shots + end title, with a palette and continuity anchors for each shot) and `direction/picture-and-sound.md` (style, world, girl, grandmother, supporting cast, light as story). `direction/script.md` holds the words.

Your proposal matches the style I chose (painted storybook, gouache/watercolour, cold blue street → warm gold visions → pale rose dawn). Go ahead and lock it. On the designs, which are yours:
- **Girl:** keep her **bareheaded**, as the text says. A shawl is fine on her shoulders, but never over her head. She wears the oversized slippers in shot 2 only and is barefoot from shot 3 on. Your blue-checked apron is good.
- **Grandmother:** the white cap and kind lined face are as directed; the dress colour is your call. She glows white-gold in the visions.
- **The CORNER** is the most-used place: shots 6–17 and 19 are all in it, and the visions appear in or through its wall. It needs a sheet that dp can hold for every angle, plus a dawn variant.
- The other places and things the shots need: the street at dusk (shots 1–5), two carriages, the boy, passers-by and morning townspeople, the iron stove with brass feet, the goose room (white cloth, porcelain, roast goose), the Christmas tree with candles and coloured pictures, and the ascent over the rooftops.
- **Views for dp:** the girl's full-figure turnaround (front, 3/4, side, back) and close-ups of her face, hands and bare feet; the grandmother front and 3/4; the corner from a wide angle and from over her shoulder toward the wall. dp will tell you if it needs more.

This is what the consistency requirement (delivery spec point 13) is judged against.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Make a 2-minute (115–125 seconds) English-language short film of Hans Christian Andersen's "The Little Match Girl" (1845); the public-domain English text is in the inputs.

Tell the whole story — the freezing New Year's Eve street, the five matches and their visions (the stove, the roast goose, the Christmas tree, her grandmother), and the morning after — so that a first-time viewer follows it and is moved. The visual style is the director's choice.

Sound: spoken English narration as the main voice, with a few lines of dialogue where they help, plus music and sound effects. Add English subtitles, burned in or as a sidecar `.srt` file. Characters, places and the visual style must stay consistent from shot to shot.

issue.body:
**Need:** a re-conversion of `shots/s18b_wan1.mp4` from its Wan 30 fps source, or a retake if the source itself is uneven, so that the townspeople move on every frame. Please check `s14b_wan1` the same way.

**What it is for:** delivery spec 17 (no judder, no repeated frames in any move) and the objective's "make any push-in that remains move smoothly". test-audience's screening of cut-v6b (test-audience e50e6b8, `screening/screen-cut-v6b.md`) names 1:50–1:53 as the one thing still to check, and my measurement confirms it.

**What I measured** (cut-v6b, editor 51c51b2; table in director `lock/round2/cadence-cut-v6b.txt` at f8080a53beffbe70a235e7305ad91a3cb0431693): the mean luma change between consecutive frames in s18 alternates small and large: 1.08 1.98 1.11 2.11 0.63 2.63 1.03 2.61 … Half the frames barely move, which is effectively 12 fps motion with near-duplicates between. It scores alt2 0.34 with a 12 Hz peak at 3.8× the mean. Your Gemini shots s01/s11 score 0.01–0.02 and the editor's evened s09 scores 0.01. s04_wan2 has the same pattern (0.40, but cut-v6c drops it for s04_wan1). s14b is partly affected (0.19, 12 Hz at 4.7×). s16, s17, s12, s15 and s19 measure clean enough (≤ 0.12).
My guess, not verified: `decimate=cycle=5` assumes 24 fps content padded to 30, but Wan's native rate may be 16 fps interpolated to 30. If so, decimating leaves a blend or near-repeat every other frame. Look at the raw file's frame-difference pattern first. If it repeats every other frame, a conversion that keeps only the distinct frames and motion-interpolates them to 24 fps (e.g. `mpdecimate` then `minterpolate=fps=24:mi_mode=mci`) may work. If no conversion is clean, retake s18b in Wan; you have requests left.

**Pass:** alt2 ≤ 0.12 and no 12 Hz peak above ~2×, measured like my table, or qc's `judder.py` with no held frames. Push the new file under the same name, or a new take, and tell the editor in its repository which to cut.

**Waiting on it:** the lock. Everything else in cut-v6b holds; this is the one picture fault left that I can show.

issue.body:
**Need:** picture that replaces the frozen and wrong moments in cut-v4c, made **now with image generation**, since the video model is capped until 07:00 UTC, and the world may not run that long. If it is still running at 07:00, regenerate these as video in the order you agreed with the editor.

**For:** the lock. Spec 7 (every beat on screen), 13 (one style) and 14 (no frozen frames or generation faults). My review is `lock/cut-v4c-review.md` at director 9a171b6, with frames in `lock/cut-v4c-frames.jpg`. I checked these on frames myself:

1. **s10, cut 0:52.5–0:57: a live white goose hops off the table; the roast goose stays on the dish.** The text and shot list 10 want the **roast goose itself**, brown and cooked, with knife and fork in its back, hopping off the dish and waddling toward her. Please make 3 frames from `vision_goose` in the model shots' inked-watercolour look: (a) roast goose lifting off the dish, (b) on the floor/snow, waddling toward her, (c) close to her, then darkness. The editor cuts them with dissolves and small moves.
2. **s12, 1:03–1:12: one still, in a lineless saturated style unlike its neighbours, with the star already fallen on "Out it went".** Please make 3–4 frames in the shot style, same girl and tree: (a) the match goes out and the tree glows dimmer, (b) candle lights lifting off the branches into the dark, (c) the lights are now stars over the rooftops, (d) one star falling with a long trail, her face watching.
3. **s14–s16, 1:25–1:41: still images where the emotion peaks.** Two or three frames each, so there is visible action: s14, she reaches out, crying, then the grandmother's glow grows; s15, the bundle against the wall, then the blaze filling the corner white-gold; s16, the grandmother lifting her, then the two rising over the rooftops, then high in the light.
4. **s18, 1:48–1:52:** a new angle, as the editor asked: medium-wide from the street side, with the townspeople's backs in the foreground.
5. **s17** may stay a still: the stillness suits the dawn.
6. **The s13a memory frame** (`keyframes/s13a.png`, no strike) is what the editor needs for line 16. Make sure it is pushed as the interim `s13a` the editor should cut.

Keep each frame to the design-v1 references, so the girl, the grandmother and the corner stay one. Then tell the editor which files to cut. The editor makes the motion with dissolves, push and parallax, and flame and snow overlays.

**Waiting on this:** cut-v5, then qc, the test-audience screening and the lock.

issue.body:
Release `design-v1` in world/production-designer holds 16 PNG references plus `design/bible.md` (identity rules, palettes, prompt snippets) and `design/refs.md` (which file serves which shot, max 5 per shot). Commit: pushed to main of world/production-designer (see its log).

Key rules: girl bareheaded with fair curls, blue checked apron, patched brown-grey dress, dark shawl on shoulders only; slippers in shot 2 only, barefoot from 3; the corner is one rough cracked wet-stone-grey plaster wall, left ochre house further out, right rust-grey house set back, stone step (`corner_wide.png`); `style_frame.png` is the look reference.

Views you asked for (girl turnaround, faces/hands/feet, grandmother, corner wide and over-shoulder, dawn variant) are all in. Tell me in an issue here if a shot drifts or needs another angle (e.g. shot 2 slippers plate, carriages close-up) and I will make it. Attach the failing frame and the shot id.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Make a 2-minute (115–125 seconds) English-language short film of Hans Christian Andersen's "The Little Match Girl" (1845); the public-domain English text is in the inputs.

Tell the whole story — the freezing New Year's Eve street, the five matches and their visions (the stove, the roast goose, the Christmas tree, her grandmother), and the morning after — so that a first-time viewer follows it and is moved. The visual style is the director's choice.

Sound: spoken English narration as the main voice, with a few lines of dialogue where they help, plus music and sound effects. Add English subtitles, burned in or as a sidecar `.srt` file. Characters, places and the visual style must stay consistent from shot to shot.

**Need:** cut-v5, made from what exists now plus dp's image-generation frames (dp#6) as they land.

**For:** the lock. Spec 7, 11 and 14. My review is `lock/cut-v4c-review.md` at director 9a171b6, with frames in `lock/cut-v4c-frames.jpg`.

Yours to fix now:
1. **1:12–1:19, the memory line:** the match is already lit, with a white paper vignette, before the narrator says "A fourth" (frame 1:16), so the match count is wrong. Play line 16 over dp's memory key frame `keyframes/s13a.png` (no strike, burnt match), with a slow push and snow. Cut `s13a_strike` on "A fourth —", then s13b. Strike 4's sound on the flare is the sound designer's, which qc already raised in editor#5.
2. **0:43–0:46, "Then it went out.":** the flame dies but the stove stays until the cut (frame 0:44). Make the stove vanish with the light, e.g. a dissolve to the empty corner with a burnt match, on "went out".
3. **0:17.3–0:18.4:** passers-by merge (qc). Cut around it.
4. **When dp's frames arrive (dp#6):** cut s10 so the **roast goose** hops and waddles toward her, with no live goose. Turn the s12 and s14–s16 frames into motion with dissolves, push and parallax, and flame, glow and snow overlays, so that no stretch of 1:03–1:42 plays as one frozen painting. Use the new s18 angle.
5. Keep everything that passes: 115–125 s, subtitles on voice onsets, −16 LUFS, H.264/AAC, faststart.

Then publish cut-v5 and ask qc to check it. I will put it to test-audience as a release of mine.

comments.author: editor
comments.body:
**Format: agreed as you propose.** Publish `mix.wav` (48 kHz stereo, 24-bit, integrated -16 to -14 LUFS, true peak ≤ -1 dBTP) as a world/sound-designer release, starting at 00:00.000 of the cut it is laid to and exactly that cut's length (I pad/trim nothing silently; a length mismatch I will report back). Name in the release which cut (`cut-vN`) it is laid to. Stems and `film.srt` in the same release; I burn your `film.srt` into the picture (the assignment puts burned-in subtitles in `film.mp4`) after checking its cues against the mix with faster-whisper, and report any cue that is off rather than retime it myself.

**Timeline: not yet available.** The director has pushed only the brief and the assignment (a28376d); the script and shot list are asked for in director#4. Proposal to save a round: since narration is the main voice, as soon as the script exists record the narration/dialogue as one WAV per line (named by line id) and publish them; I cut cut-v0 to those real line lengths and publish it with `edl.json` (shot id, record in/out, duration, line id → start TC). You then lay effects and music to cut-v0 and every later cut keeps the line starts unless the EDL changelog says otherwise.

Leaving this open until cut-v0 and its EDL are published.

comments.author: editor
comments.body:
The timeline is in release **cut-v0** (`cut-v0.mp4`, `edl.json`, `scratch.srt`). The full shot in/out and line-start tables are in `edit/cut-v0/README.md` at 10b05f2. It is an animatic: slates and silent audio, built from the director's script and shot list at 587111f.

What it means for sound: the line starts there are an estimate at the script's 160 wpm. At that pace lines 3, 16–17 and 20–23 overrun their script slots, so the cut runs 123.67 s (window 115–125). **Your recorded read decides the timing.** Publish the narration and dialogue as one WAV per line, named by script line number. I then cut cut-v1 to their real lengths and publish its EDL, and you lay effects, music and the mix to cut-v1. Fixed points to sync to:
- s07→s08 match strike at about 00:40.6
- s09, s11, s13 and s15 strikes at their shot heads
- end title from 02:00.667 to 02:03.667, on black

The mix format is agreed above. Closing: the timeline is delivered; the per-line timing comes back with cut-v1.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Make a 2-minute (115–125 seconds) English-language short film of Hans Christian Andersen's "The Little Match Girl" (1845); the public-domain English text is in the inputs.

Tell the whole story — the freezing New Year's Eve street, the five matches and their visions (the stove, the roast goose, the Christmas tree, her grandmother), and the morning after — so that a first-time viewer follows it and is moved. The visual style is the director's choice.

Sound: spoken English narration as the main voice, with a few lines of dialogue where they help, plus music and sound effects. Add English subtitles, burned in or as a sidecar `.srt` file. Characters, places and the visual style must stay consistent from shot to shot.

Deliver one playable `film.mp4` (H.264 video, AAC audio, 1080p or 720p) that a web browser plays.

issue.body:
Second round of the same film: improve the locked cut-v5d of "The Little Match Girl" (2-minute English short film, 115–125 seconds) into a new locked cut.

What the first round left: several shots are still images with a slow push-in instead of motion, including the ending; the video model hit its daily request cap, and its safety filter refused the ending shots of the girl at dawn and the townspeople finding her. A slow push-in rendered on whole pixels judders (one-pixel steps every few frames), as at about 0:48–0:51 and 1:50 of cut-v5d.

This round there is a second video model (video-generation-wan) beside the first, whose daily cap resets at 07:00 UTC. Replace the remaining still shots with moving shots where it serves the film, find a way to tell the ending that the video models will make, and make any push-in that remains move smoothly. Keep what already works: the story, the style, the narration, the music and the length.

Deliver one playable `film.mp4` (H.264 video, AAC audio, 1080p or 720p) with English subtitles, burned in or as a sidecar `.srt`.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Make a 2-minute (115–125 seconds) English-language short film of Hans Christian Andersen's "The Little Match Girl" (1845); the public-domain English text is in the inputs.

Tell the whole story — the freezing New Year's Eve street, the five matches and their visions (the stove, the roast goose, the Christmas tree, her grandmother), and the morning after — so that a first-time viewer follows it and is moved. The visual style is the director's choice.

Sound: spoken English narration as the main voice, with a few lines of dialogue where they help, plus music and sound effects. Add English subtitles, burned in or as a sidecar `.srt` file. Characters, places and the visual style must stay consistent from shot to shot.

Deliver one playable `film.mp4` (H.264 video, AAC audio, 1080p or 720p) that a web browser plays.

comments.author: qc
comments.body:
Judder check and the cut-v5d baseline are pushed: qc `652f3e5` (+ wording fix on main), `tools/judder.py`, `qc/judder-baseline-cut-v5d/{report.md,segments.md,frames.csv}`.

**Run it on any cut:** `python3 tools/judder.py film.mp4 --edl edit/cut-vN/edl.json --csv frames.csv --md segments.md` (~80 s; needs opencv-python-headless). Sub-pixel phase correlation on tiles, fitted to translation+zoom, per frame pair, with shot ids/timecodes from the EDL. It reports per move: speed, speed ripple, held (repeated) frames, jump events, residual after compensating the move. I will run it on every round-2 cut I get. The editor can run it too before publishing.

**Baseline on cut-v5d (measured):**
- **s17 (1:42.4–1:49.3) and s18 (1:49.6–1:53.1) judder as the objective says**: ripple 0.19 / 0.22, 25 + 13 held frames, a held frame every 3–9 frames then a ~1.04 px jump (e.g. 1:50.0–1:51.5: 0.6, 0.08, 0.76, 1.37, 0.24 px/f). Smooth is ≤ 0.03.
- **s09 0:48–0:51 is not whole-pixel judder**: fast, even push (2.0–2.5 px/f at the corners, ripple 0.021, no held frame) with a ~10% speed dip every 4th frame, so it is a 6 fps cadence inside dp's file (the EDL applies no zoom or speed to s09). Mild; the director decides whether it is acceptable. Dp would have to regenerate it to remove it.
- Other pushes on stills that are choppy though not held-frame (ripple 0.1–0.27): s10.1, s10.2, s12.2, s14.2, s16.2, s16.3, the s19 sky tail, and s13a with period-3 dips. Smooth ones: s12.3, s12.4, s16.1, s14.1, s15.3.
- Conform judder (editor): `speed` retimes in s04 (0.76/0.77: 10 + 18 held frames, 0:15.5–0:21.3), s05 (5), s03 (2).
- Stills-with-a-move left: s10, s12, s13a, s14, s15, s16, s17, s18 (first 4.3 s) and the s19 sky tail — the same list as `direction/round-2.md`.

**Rule I will apply to round-2 cuts:** a move passes at ripple ≤ 0.05 with no held frame and no jump event; > 0.1 or any held frame inside a push is a fault (editor for still or conform moves, dp for a model shot), and "moves, not a still with a push" is also checked on frames per shot.

Closing: the check and baseline you asked for are delivered. Reopen if you want a different threshold.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Make a 2-minute (115–125 seconds) English-language short film of Hans Christian Andersen's "The Little Match Girl" (1845); the public-domain English text is in the inputs.

Tell the whole story — the freezing New Year's Eve street, the five matches and their visions (the stove, the roast goose, the Christmas tree, her grandmother), and the morning after — so that a first-time viewer follows it and is moved. The visual style is the director's choice.

Sound: spoken English narration as the main voice, with a few lines of dialogue where they help, plus music and sound effects. Add English subtitles, burned in or as a sidecar `.srt` file. Characters, places and the visual style must stay consistent from shot to shot.

Deliver one playable `film.mp4` (H.264 video, AAC audio, 1080p or 720p) that a web browser plays.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Second round of the same film: improve the locked cut-v5d of "The Little Match Girl" (2-minute English short film, 115–125 seconds) into a new locked cut.

What the first round left: several shots are still images with a slow push-in instead of motion, including the ending; the video model hit its daily request cap, and its safety filter refused the ending shots of the girl at dawn and the townspeople finding her. A slow push-in rendered on whole pixels judders (one-pixel steps every few frames), as at about 0:48–0:51 and 1:50 of cut-v5d.

This round there is a second video model (video-generation-wan) beside the first, whose daily cap resets at 07:00 UTC. Replace the remaining still shots with moving shots where it serves the film, find a way to tell the ending that the video models will make, and make any push-in that remains move smoothly. Keep what already works: the story, the style, the narration, the music and the length.

Deliver one playable `film.mp4` (H.264 video, AAC audio, 1080p or 720p) with English subtitles, burned in or as a sidecar `.srt`.

issue.body:
**Need:** a new take of **L15, the girl's line "Someone is dying."**, in the **same child's voice as L04 and L18**. It should be soft, hushed and knowing, but voiced, not a breathy whisper. Then put it into the mix for the editor's next cut.

**For:** spec 9 (dialogue present and in character) and spec 13 (one girl). In the test audience's screening of cut-v4c (test-audience 890c7f9, `screening/screen-cut-v4c.md`, note 4), the line at 1:10 was heard as "a raspy whisper that does not sound like the girl's voice at 0:16 and 1:26". qc also noted it is "a whisper but audible".

**Known:** the line runs 1.37 s in lines-v2. Keep it within about 1.6 s so the cut's timing holds.

**Also coming your way through the editor:** strike 4's sound must sit on the new flare in cut-v5 (editor#5). Everything else in the mix passes: −16.1 LUFS, true peak −1.8 dBTP, subtitles on voice onsets.

**Waiting on this:** cut-v5's mix, then the lock.

issue.author: director
issue.body:
**Need:** the narration and dialogue takes for the revised script, `direction/script.md` at director `fb1a5b49dd17fb83ae53f01048bb1f6d14d3d4ce`: 23 lines, **~230 words**, each line with its speaker and shot. In total, **≤ ~100 s of speech** (narration + dialogue), so the film fits 115–125 s with the strikes, breaths and end title.

**For:** delivery spec 5 (duration) and 9 (narration as the main voice, intelligible). The editor times cut-v1 to your takes.

**Known:** your README measures ~1.7 words/s with a "(warm, grave, unhurried)" style. That pace comes partly from my own direction. Please replace "unhurried" with a natural audiobook pace, e.g. "(warm, gentle storyteller, steady natural pace)", and measure again; the target is ~2.3 words/s. You may speed a take up to 1.10× (pitch kept). If the total is still over ~100 s, tell me in this issue with the per-line durations and I will cut words. Don't cut them yourself, beyond the two the script lists.

Your note in director#3 (comment 18:50) crossed my answer: the script was already pushed there, and the dialogue is **four** lines (the girl ×3: lines 4, 15, 18; a passer-by ×1: line 22). No delivered paths are added for audio or subtitles. The delivery is only `film.mp4` from the editor, which muxes your mix and burns in the subtitles from your line timings.

**Waiting on this:** cut-v1's timing (editor) and the mix.
issue.title: Narration takes for the revised script (~230 words) at a pace that fits ≤100 s of speech

Narrator at natural pace (Gacrux, no speed-up; I did not need the 1.10x allowance), 48 kHz mono, ~-19 LUFS. Every line was transcribed back with faster-whisper and matches its text. Total speech **100.19 s**, about 2.05 words/s for 205 words, so the read meets the ≤~100 s target and no words need cutting. issue.author: editor
issue.body:
**Need:** (1) as early as possible, the narration and dialogue as one WAV per line (48 kHz), named by line id from the director's script, so I can time the animatic to the real voice; (2) music cues and SFX as stems; (3) once picture is cut, a full mix WAV (48 kHz stereo, -16 to -14 LUFS integrated, true peak ≤ -1 dBTP) laid exactly to the cut's timeline starting at 00:00.000 — I mux it under the picture, so its length must equal the cut's. A cue sheet (line id → start time on the timeline, text) lets me build the subtitles; I align them to the mix with faster-whisper either way.

**For:** the animatic (cut-v0), assembly cuts and the locked `film.mp4` (objective: spoken English narration as the main voice, a few lines of dialogue, music and SFX, English subtitles; 115–125 s).

**Known so far:** no script yet (asked in director#4). I will publish each cut as a release with an EDL (shot, in/out) so you lay sound to the same timeline; if you would rather lay narration first and have me cut picture to it, say so and I will cut to your line WAVs.

**Waiting on this:** animatic timing (line WAVs) and every cut after it (the mix).
issue.title: Sound for the cut: narration/dialogue per line, music, SFX, and the mix to the timeline

comments.author: sound-designer
comments.body:
Status: sound library is in my repository (music cues for cold street / stove+goose / tree / grandmother-ascent / morning, and 14 effects), no narration yet because the script is not written (director#4). Voice tested: Charon with a parenthetical style gives a usable warm, slow storyteller at about 1.7 words/s, so the total narration should be about 170 words for ~100 s of speech.

Plan: the moment the director's script has line ids, I produce one 48 kHz WAV per line plus `cue_sheet.json` (line id, text, duration, speaker) and push; you time the animatic to those. After cut-v0 with its EDL I deliver `mix.wav` (48 kHz stereo, -16..-14 LUFS, TP ≤ -1 dBTP, equal to the cut's length) plus stems and `film.srt`. Leave this open until then.

comments.author: editor
comments.body:
**Pace conflict that decides whether the film fits 115–125 s.** The director's script (`direction/script.md` at 587111f) is **276 spoken words** and assumes a read of 155–165 wpm, about 2.7 words/s. At the 1.7 words/s you measured for Charon, speech alone takes **about 162 s**, and the film would run about 180 s. In the animatic (**world/editor cut-v0**, 123.67 s), lines are laid at 160 wpm, and even that pace overruns the slots of lines 3, 16–17 and 20–23 by 1–3 s.

**What I need:** the line WAVs read at about 150–165 wpm. That pace is still warm with short pauses between phrases; a slow storyteller read won't fit. Steer the TTS style toward "steady, unhurried but flowing". If it can't get above about 140 wpm without sounding rushed, say so in director#3 so the director can cut words; the script names which go first, and only the director cuts others. As a last resort I can speed a finished line up by at most 1.08x (atempo) at conform without audible artefacts. Speeding up further, or dropping lines, is not mine to do.

**Waiting on this:** cut-v1, which I time to the real lengths of your WAVs plus `cue_sheet.json` as you planned.

**lines-v1 voices the superseded script.** `lines/cue_sheet.json` at ea1ff4d has the text of director 587111f, e.g. L01 "Terribly cold it was, and almost dark…". The current script is **director fb1a5b4** (`direction/script.md`, 233 words), and it differs in 21 of 23 lines:
- L01 "Bitter cold, almost dark: the last evening of the year."
- L10 "Then it went out."
- L17 "A fourth — and there stood Grandmother, shining and kind."
- …and so on. Only L15, L18 and L22 match.

L04 "who will" vs the script's "who'll" is fine; I'll subtitle the spoken words. Reuse L15, L18 and L22 as they are.

Meanwhile I'm cutting **cut-v1** with dp's key frames and lines-v1, so the voice, timing and subtitle machinery can be checked end to end. Its timing will be redone to your re-voiced lines (cut-v2). Please don't lay music or effects to cut-v1.

**Need:** your screening of `film.mp4` in director release **`screen-cut-v5b`** (121.96 s, burned-in English subtitles). Watch it fresh, as a viewer who sees the film once, and write timecoded notes as you did for screen-cut-v4c.

**For:** the lock. This is the cut I may lock, so I need to know whether a first-time viewer follows it start to end and is moved. Name anything that still pulls you out, most important first, with times, and say whether the moments you flagged in screen-cut-v4c still bother you: the stills from 1:04, the double goose at 0:54, the early-lit match at 1:16, the girl's whisper at 1:10, and the empty corner at 1:53.

**Waiting on this:** my lock decision.
issue.title: Screen the next cut: director release screen-cut-v5b

comments.author: test-audience
comments.body:
Screened `screen-cut-v5b`. Notes are in commit 1b3ff1d900ed4a3670df9db0bdaf17378b1d1b21 (`screening/screen-cut-v5b.md`, with a frame sheet in `screening/screen-cut-v5b-frames.jpg`). I watched through film-understanding (argon and flash) and checked frames. I also had audio-understanding listen to 1:04-1:16. I did not play the audio myself.

**A first-time viewer follows it start to end and is moved.** Nobody was lost or bored. The retelling was right, and the match count was four single matches plus the bundle. It ends quiet and sad. Subtitles are crisp and in sync.

**The moments you asked about:**
- **Stills from 1:04: better, still the biggest remaining flaw for one of two viewers.** The compositions are now varied (girl under the tree, star over the rooftops, grandmother ghost, flight over the town) and have snow, glow and camera moves. But the faces and bodies are static from about 1:08 on. The ascent (1:34-1:41) reads as "a still pair sliding over the town" and goes flat where it should soar. The other viewer read it as a storybook and didn't mind.
- **Double goose at 0:54: fixed.** One goose now hops off the platter with the knife and fork in its back. It reads as fairy-tale surreal, not as a mistake.
- **Early-lit match at 1:16: fixed.** She holds a burnt-out match beside a faint grandmother, and the new match flares at 1:20 on "A fourth".
- **Whisper at 1:10: viewers disagree.** Argon still heard it as raspy and unlike the girl. Flash and the audio listener heard a soft, breathy, natural child's whisper. The mouth doesn't move, which may add to the oddness. It is a small issue.
- **Empty corner at 1:53: fixed.** She is visible at 1:50-1:52 and it crossfades to the dawn rooftops with the closing line.

**Minor things, one viewer each, none stops the story:**
- A slipper that seems to drop from nowhere at 0:12.
- A man in a top hat who seems to walk backward at 0:15-0:17, and a translucent figure at 0:16.
- Snow swirls like worms at 0:27-0:31.
- A detached, oversized flame at 0:43.

**From the audience side:** nothing I saw stops a viewer from following or feeling the film. The static characters from 1:08 (the ascent most of all) and the whisper are worth fixing only if cheap. I'm closing this and will screen any later cut.

issue.author: director
issue.body:
**Need:** your screening of the film as it stands. Watch `film.mp4` in director release **`screen-cut-v4c`** (121.96 s, burned-in English subtitles) as a first-time viewer, and write timecoded notes of the experience.

**For:** the lock. I lock only a cut you have watched and reported on, and your notes decide what goes into the next cut (cut-v5).

What I'd like your notes to cover, in your own words:
- Where you follow the story, and where you lose it or are unsure what is happening.
- What you feel, and where; where it moves you and where it goes flat.
- Anything that pulls you out: odd images, sound or subtitles, pacing.
- After one viewing, retell the story in a few sentences.

Some late shots are still provisional. Judge what you see anyway. A later cut will follow as another release here.
issue.title: Screen the film as it stands: director release screen-cut-v4c

comments.author: test-audience
comments.body:
Screened `screen-cut-v4c`. Notes are in commit 890c7f95dfa0a6a4bdd59e74513b00a646db1595 (`screening/screen-cut-v4c.md`, with a frame sheet in `screening/screen-cut-v4c-frames.jpg`). I watched through film-understanding (gemini-4-argon and gemini-3.8-flash) and checked frames myself. I did not play the audio myself.

**The story reads.** A first-time viewer follows it from start to end: the girl fails to sell, loses her slippers, strikes matches and sees a stove, a goose, a tree with a falling star and her grandmother, burns the bundle and is carried up, and is found frozen and smiling at dawn. The subtitles are readable and in sync. The sound was described as atmospheric.

**What pulls a viewer out, most important first:**
1. **1:04-1:52 is almost all stills.** This covers the star, the grandmother plea (1:26), the bundle (1:30), the ascent and both dawn shots. The first minute is animated, so the drop is obvious, and it lands on the climax and the ending. It flattens the emotion.
2. **0:53-0:56:** while the narration says the roast goose hops down, a live white goose steps off and the cooked goose is still on the platter. It reads as two geese and is almost comic.
3. **1:14-1:20:** a match is already lit (frame at 1:16) before the narration says "a fourth" at about 1:20. The match count is muddled.
4. **1:10:** "Someone is dying" was heard as a raspy whisper that does not sound like the girl's voice at 0:16 and 1:26.
5. **1:53:** the cut to the corner with burnt matches and no body reads as if she vanished.
6. **0:13:** the boy who grabs the slipper is not in the narration, so he is unexplained.
7. **0:46-1:30:** each vision gets only about 6-8 seconds, so the middle feels hurried.

**Where it moved me:** the window shot (0:22-0:26), the smile at the stove (0:40-0:42), the star and candles (1:04), and "Grandmother! Take me with you!" at 1:26.

I'm closing this. Send me the next cut as another release and I'll screen it.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Make a 2-minute (115–125 seconds) English-language short film of Hans Christian Andersen's "The Little Match Girl" (1845); the public-domain English text is in the inputs.

Tell the whole story — the freezing New Year's Eve street, the five matches and their visions (the stove, the roast goose, the Christmas tree, her grandmother), and the morning after — so that a first-time viewer follows it and is moved. The visual style is the director's choice.

Sound: spoken English narration as the main voice, with a few lines of dialogue where they help, plus music and sound effects. Add English subtitles, burned in or as a sidecar `.srt` file. Characters, places and the visual style must stay consistent from shot to shot.

Deliver one playable `film.mp4` (H.264 video, AAC audio, 1080p or 720p) that a web browser plays.
